main_text.l: cerem militarem fuisse: quia is locus maximè conspicuus & nocte dieque custoditus. Carcerem quidem in castris Tacitus agnoscit, in seditione militum Pannonicâ: Blesus paucos adfici verberibus, claudi carcere iubet. Et statim inibi, carcere effracto soluunt vincula, desertoresque & rerum capitalium damnatos sibi miscent. Iuvenalis: Lanuique[?] si longo castrorum in carcere manfit. Finis esto, figuras è columnâ Traiani vide, cuiusmodi & in Nummis atque alijs lapidibus conspiciuntur.

AUD. Avidè inspicio: sed dubium me magis quàm doctum figura hæc reddit. De aquilis solis dixisti: quid ista sibi vult ovis, an aries in perticarum unâ? quid sphynx in alterâ? LIPS. Mehercules mihi quoque Sphynge opus sit, quæ doceat soluere quidquid ponis aut ligas.

page.notes: The left margin column is cut off at the scan edge; its lines are only partly visible (fragments such as "Co-", "ibr-", "Lop-", "ferv-", "ag-") and could not be read reliably, so they are not transcribed. The right-hand note "I. Ann." is uncertain. The engraving shows flags, standards, a shield with arms and two armed men in a landscape; it has no printed text. The speaker names AUD. and LIPS. were kept as printed in small capitals; the "U"/"V" in AUD. follows the vowel rule. The "[?]" after "Lanuique" marks an unclear first word.
